newsitem.title: UK: UN relations with US set to improve - Annan.
newsitem.headline: UN relations with US set to improve - Annan.

text.p: Ghana's Kofi Annan, due to become the first black African to head the United Nations, said on Sunday the world body's current poor relations with the United States were set to improve.
Annan, interviewed by the London Observer newspaper, also promised to make U.N. peacekeeping forces more robust in future.

On relations with the United States, he said: "The President (Clinton) has indicated that they will want to pay (the budget arrears of $1.5 billion) and we are getting the right noises from the Administration and Congress."

Annan, 58, was chosen by the U.N. Security Council on Friday to be the world body's next secretary-general, succeeding Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali whose hopes for a second term were derailed by Washington.

The career diplomat, currently U.N. undersecretary-general for peacekeeping operations, won the support of all 15 Security Council members after France dropped its veto threat. His selection now has to be ratified by the 185-nation General Assembly.

Reflecting on U.N. operations in Bosnia, Annan said: "We've made some mistakes. Not all our operations were successful. But there were many successful ones. In Bosnia we did make a contribution. We fed 2.5 million people through several winters and by being on the ground I hope we limited the conflict."
But he said that in future "the troops should go in and be prepared to defend their mandate and themselves and have the capacity to do so".
